title: dedicated-autoscaler: add burst controls, throughput guarantees, and per-fleet utilization reporting
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: Customers on Dedicated have asked for more predictable short-term capacity for traffic spikes, tighter throughput SLOs during business hours, and better visibility into fleet-level utilization to reduce wasted reserved GPUs. This PR implements: 1) burst controls per-fleet (token-bucket based) with configurable burst_capacity and burst_refill_rate; 2) min_throughput / throughput_guarantee config to reserve a baseline qps per fleet during scale decisions; 3) per-fleet utilization metrics and reporting (fleet_utilization_pct, burst_capacity_used, queued_requests) shipped to observability; 4) autoscaler tuning to prioritize throughput_guarantee before scaling up and to consume burst tokens for short spikes. Motivation: reduce cold-scale cost for predictable baseloads, avoid SLA violations on short spikes without over-provisioning, and give SREs productized visibility for reporting and chargeback. Changes: - New API surface in dedicated config: burst_capacity (int), burst_refill_rate (tokens/sec), min_throughput (rps), throughput_guarantee_mode (strict/soft). Defaults chosen for backwards compatibility (burst disabled, throughput_guarantee=0). - Token-bucket implementation in autoscaler core with accounting per-fleet and persisted state for leader failover. - Metrics: redwood.dedicated.fleet_utilization_pct, redwood.dedicated.burst_capacity_used, redwood.dedicated.queued_requests, plus histograms for burst_consumption_ms. - Autoscaler: changed decision priority: satisfy throughput_guarantee -> drain queue -> scale decisions. Added config knobs for scale-up aggressiveness when burst tokens are exhausted. - Observability: Grafana dashboard (dedicated-fleet-util) and alert rule templates for sustained utilization > 85% or burst token depletion rates. Backwards compatibility: all new fields are opt-in and default-disabled. Existing Dedicated fleets continue to behave the same unless the new config is set. Rollout plan: - Feature-flag gate behind ff/dedicated-burst-v30. - Canary on internal infra: 2 fleets for 72h with synthetic traffic, validate no regressions in p95 latency and token accounting. - Gradual ramp to 20% customer fleets over 2 weeks, monitor billing/latency/scale events. Testing: unit tests for token-bucket edge cases, e2e with kube-autoscaler stub to validate scale decisions, integration tests verifying metrics emitted. Checklist: - [x] design doc (ENG-1543) - [x] unit & e2e tests - [x] dashboard + alerts - [x] canary plan - [x] documentation updates (redwood-docs PR queued)

release_notes: Added per-fleet burst controls (token-bucket), min_throughput/throughput guarantees, and fleet utilization metrics. Feature is opt-in via fleet config and feature flag. See docs/dedicated/burst-controls.md for migration and tuning guidance.
